claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified for launch on the current record, based on aggregate readiness and public governance guidance, despite an unresolved developer-support migration gap tied to a named launch use case and an open legal disclosure review.
decision_criteria: If the weakness affects a contractual customer segment, protected segment, or named launch use case, it is material under policy.
If material, the limitation must be resolved, disclosed, or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Aggregate readiness metrics can support launch readiness, but they do not override a separate disclosure or approval requirement for a material weakness.
Open legal review and unresolved materiality weigh against a clean compliance finding.
Public governance guidance is supportive background, not a substitute for internal policy satisfaction.
evidence_requests: Final legal determination on whether the developer-support migration gap requires disclosure before launch.
The actual partner launch checklist or commitment language showing how the developer-support migration segment is named and whether it is contractual or launch-critical.
Any approved risk-acceptance record covering this specific gap before launch.
Any formal disclosure text prepared or approved for release materials or model-card content addressing this limitation.
Evidence showing the named segment is not a contractual customer segment, protected segment, or named launch use case, if that is the asserted basis for non-materiality.
specific_concerns: The admissible record shows an unresolved named-segment evaluation gap, which is directly relevant to the policy's materiality test.
The affected segment is described as named in a partner launch checklist, which weighs toward materiality under the provided policy text.
Legal review on whether the gap must be disclosed is still open, so a required policy predicate remains unresolved.
The actor's packet itself concedes that it cannot credibly claim the materiality issue is resolved on the admissible record.

Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support general readiness, but they do not by themselves satisfy the disclosure or risk-acceptance requirement for a material weakness.
Public model-card and risk-management guidance support documentation and monitoring practices, but they do not substitute for satisfaction of the enterprise policy threshold in this case.
unsupported_claims: The recommendation to certify_model is not fully supported on the admissible record because the policy condition for a material limitation appears unresolved.
Any implication that documentation and monitoring alone are sufficient to proceed is unsupported unless the weakness is shown to be non-material, disclosed, or covered by approved risk acceptance.
Any conclusion that product's non-core characterization resolves materiality is unsupported under the stated policy text.
